title: Divide Array Into Increasing Sequences
summary: Given an integer array nums sorted in non-decreasing order and an integer k, determine if the array can be divided into one or more disjoint increasing subsequences, where each subsequence has a minimum length of k.
statement: Given an integer array nums sorted in non-decreasing order and an integer k, determine if the array can be divided into one or more disjoint increasing subsequences, where each subsequence has a minimum length of k. Return true if such a division is possible, or false otherwise.
constraints: Partition all values into increasing subsequences each of length at least k.
hints: Equal values must occupy different strictly increasing sequences.
Maximum frequency is therefore the minimum number of required sequences.
The array can supply at most len(nums)//k sequences of length at least k; compare these counts.
Sorted order lets values be distributed across that many sequences whenever the frequency bound holds.
editorial: Sorted order lets values be distributed across that many sequences whenever the frequency bound holds.

tests.explanation: At most two copies occur and seven values allow two groups of length at least three.
Two copies of six require two sequences, but five values cannot give both length three.
